I am an old man now, 84 years, and my strength is not what it was. This small plot near my home is where I grow my maize with some pumpkins and beans between the rows, the way we have always done. I will try to buy a little fertilizer if the subsidy coupon reaches me, but money is tight so I cannot afford much, and I will put some manure from my few chickens and goats around the planting stations. My children and grandchildren help me with the digging and weeding because my back cannot manage alone, and I rely on the rains from the sky — there is no river or pump here for me.
